See my comment here https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/25299#issuecomment-463394298, I think we should separately try to fix it using `numeric_only` (would you want to do that here?), and then think about deprecating it (see https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/25303)

@arnov Thanks for the updates! 
But, as I said above, I think it would be better to keep the numeric_only fix, and the deprecation separate. The deprecation is only for 0.25.0, but the regression fix would be good to include in version 0.24.2

@jorisvandenbossche yes, sorry! I've made this one simpler and kept only the fix for numeric_only. I've kept the other changes in another branch, so could make a separate PR out of that after this one is done.

Two further questions:

- can you add a note in the 0.24.2 whatsnew file? (in the regression section)
- workflow related: in general, we prefer that you push new commits to a PR, instead of squashing/amending a previous commit and force pushing. That way it makes it easier to eg see what changed since a last review (in this case not that important of course since it is a very small diff), and we squash/merge PRs in the end anyway, so it is no problem that there are multiple (unclean) commits in the PR branch.

Moving this discussion out of the review comment (https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/25304#discussion_r257208313) to keep it easier to follow. 
Discussion is about where to add the special casing for the `numeric_only` keyword for Categorical: in `Series._reduce` or in `Categorical`. Adding it in `Series._reduce` is less clean (but only temporary), but moving it to `Categorical` would mean that the `EA._reduce` in general needs to accept (and ignore) the `numeric_only`. Which would be an API change.

But to take a step back: @jreback do you agree that in the _long term_ we can deprecate this `numeric_only` keyword for Categorical.min/max?
(it's the only EA that now uses it, while the others all use `skipna` for the same thing)

> But to take a step back: @jreback do you agree that in the _long term_ we can deprecate this `numeric_only` keyword for Categorical.min/max?
(it's the only EA that now uses it, while the others all use `skipna` for the same this

not sure what you mean here. The ``numeric_only`` kwarg is pretty generic an ingrained. I think you need to accept it for ``Catetogorical`` and either ignore it or handle it. EA's can choose to respond to this or not. But this is a higher level operation, applying to each array in turn.
Again, please read  #25303, and respond there is you don't agree or don't understand the reasoning. This is *not* about the general `numeric_only` keyword.

OK, so we agree that, in the long term, we want to deprecate and remove `numeric_only` from `Categorical.min/max`.

To fix the regression (what this PR is doing), we still have to deal with this special case until it is finally removed. 
So either we need to *change* the public API of `EA._reduce`, or either we agree to have the special case in `Series._reduce` (we are talking about *two lines* of code), which is what this PR is doing.

Changing the public API will lead to more changes internally than 2 lines, but moreover is something we should IMO not do for a bug fix release. So @jreback short-term proposal: we do it as in this PR for 0.24.2, and discuss / re-work it for 0.25.0 ?

issue_context.title: Minimum of ordered categorical data in Panda DataFrames
issue_context.body:
I have a Pandas DataFrame with one Serie containing ordered Categorical data. Some value of this Serie may be missing (NaN). I want to get the minimum without taking into account NaNs but I obtained strange results ...

#### Code:
```python
raw_cat = pd.Categorical(["a", "b", "c", "a"],
                         categories=["b", "c", "d"],
                         ordered=True)
s = pd.Series(raw_cat)
raw_cat.min(numeric_only=True), s.min(numeric_only=True)
```
#### Output:
```python
('b', nan)
```
#### Expected utput:
```python
('b', 'b')
```

I am getting the desired output when running this code with pandas 0.23.4 but not with pandas 0.24.0 and above.

Is this an issue or a misunderstanding? Thank you for your help.
comments: Thanks for the report! I can confirm this regression.
So it seems that the `numeric_only` keyword is no longer properly passed through to the Categorical.min implementation. Investigation welcome!
I dove into this a bit, but shouldn't the argument be `skipna`? Because I am unsure what `numeric_only` would mean for a categorical series.
I agree with you ! It makes no sense to use this argument while the argument used to removed NaNs in all other Pandas' methods is `skipna` ...
To add to the confusion, `Categorical` supports the `dropna` argument in the `mode` method, while it seems to be `skipna` in a lot of other places.

review_comments: these should go with the categorical tests not here

Jeff, please looks at the rest of the test. This addition is very logical here (it is about categorical Series, not Categorical). Inside the categorical tests, there are no tests for Series[categorical].min(). That is only tested in the test above.
at the very least make this a new test name

why are u adding a code path here? the original is much more generic ; need to avoid special cases like this
if u need to handle this specially then the place is in the Categirical itself

This is because Categorical deviates here from the standard ExtensionArray (see https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/25303 for the issue about that). 
I personally find it clearer with this special case, making it explicit that Categorical has a different signature. And after the deprecation period, we can remove this special case.

If you feel strongly about it, it can indeed be handled inside Categorical. But that means that all the other arrays' `_reduce` method needs to be updated as well to handle (=ignore) `numeric_only`, which is also not clean (and the special case here is only temporarily anyway).

this is not more clear and leads to future issues
pls move to _reduce
not sure why the others need to change at all you’re logic is circular

This would cause more changes, since the problem is actually that the argument `numeric_only` is not passed currently. If we would add it for every `ExtensionArray` call we get problems at the other reduction methods. For instance here: https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/master/pandas/core/arrays/numpy_.py#L322 (they don't have `numeric_only`, or `**kwargs` in the method definition). 

So we could change the call for every `ExtenensionArray` to:

`return delegate._reduce(name, skipna=skipna, numeric_only=numeric_only, **kwds)`

but then we would need to make sure every child of ExtensionArray supports this and this is currently not the case.

@arnov explained it well. I think we don't want to change the EA interface (`_reduce` is an official part of it) just for this back-compat special case we are going to deprecate. Hence, categorical needs to be handled separately here (but again, this is only temporary)

disagree numeric_only is likely not going away anytime soon and even so
the EA simply need to accept it (they can ignore it)

@jreback this is *not* about the numeric_only in DataFrame/Series reductions that determines for which columns the reduction is calculated. This is another meaning of  the keyword *only* for categorical that determines whether NaNs should be skipped or not. Please read https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/25303

So we are not speaking about removing that general use case of `numeric_only`, but only the one in Categorical.min/max.

i’ll look closer but am still -1 on any handling as a special case in the Series call
the point is that pass on kwargs; EA can ignore or not as required

OK, to take a step back: @jreback do you agree that in the *long term* we can deprecate this `numeric_only` keyword for Categorical.min/max? 
(it's the only EA that now uses it, while the others all use `skipna` for the same thing)
